title: Hand tools, PPE and safe work area
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: Safe Work Australia, How to manage work health and safety risks: Code of Practice (dated December 2011, shown in document).
audience: Handyman workers and property maintenance workers
learningOutcomes: Select a hand tool that suits the fastener, the substrate and the task.
Inspect hand tools and reject any that are defective.
Set up and keep a safe work area with protection matched to the task risks.

instruction.heading: Match the tool to the job
instruction.body: A hand tool is safe when it is the right tool for the fastener, the material and the force required. A screwdriver used as a chisel, or a spanner used as a hammer, may slip or break and cause injury. Before you start, identify the substrate (timber, plasterboard, masonry, metal), the fastener, and the force needed. Choose the tool that fits the fastener head exactly and that gives control. Use a pilot hole or a suitable bit rather than forcing a fixing.

instruction.heading: Inspect before use
instruction.body: Inspect each tool before it goes into use. Reject a hammer with a mushroomed striking face or a loose head. Reject a screwdriver with a rounded or cracked tip. Reject a wrench with splayed jaws. Reject a handle that is split, loose or greasy, and any cutting tool with a damaged edge that cannot be sharpened safely on site. A rejected tool is tagged out of service and removed from the work area. Do not compensate for a faulty tool with extra force, because that is when the tool fails.

instruction.heading: Work area and personal protection
instruction.body: Keep the work area clear of trip hazards, cords and loose material. Secure the workpiece so it cannot move while you apply force. Keep cutting edges and fingers away from the line of force. Choose eye and hand protection from the actual task risks identified in the survey, and check the protection is in good condition. Store tools in a way that stops them falling, and never leave tools on ladders, steps or window ledges where they can fall on people below.

procedure: Identify the substrate, the fastener and the force needed.
Select a tool that fits the fastener and gives control.
Inspect the tool for cracks, mushrooming, looseness, splayed jaws and damaged edges.
Tag and remove any defective tool and record it.
Secure the workpiece and clear the area of trip hazards.
Select eye and hand protection from the task risks and check it is in good condition.
Store tools safely and do not leave them at height.

workedExamples.situation: An adjustable wrench has splayed jaws, and the job is almost finished.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the wrench be used to finish the job?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Splayed jaws can slip off the fastener and injure a hand or damage the fitting. Tag the wrench out of service, replace it with a sound tool, and record the defect. Using extra force to compensate is the main cause of slips with worn tools.

equipmentAndPpe: Basic hand tools: screwdrivers, spanners, hammers, pliers, utility knife, tape measure
Safety glasses and cut-resistant gloves selected for the task
Tool bag or rack for safe storage
Tag and tag-out record for defective tools

commonErrors.error: Using a worn or damaged tool because it is nearly finished.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect before each use and tag out any defective tool.

commonErrors.error: Using the wrong tool because the right one is not on hand.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop and get the right tool. Do not improvise with a tool that is not designed for the task.

commonErrors.error: Leaving tools on a ladder or window ledge.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep tools in a bag or on a tray, and never leave them at height.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Hand tool selection and inspection are good-practice controls that sit within the general duty to manage risk in Safe Work Australia's model code of practice (dated December 2011). They do not depend on any licence and do not alter any licence position.
Any task that moves into a licensed trade, such as wiring a fitting or working on a gas appliance, is outside this lesson and must be referred under “Scope, consent and trade boundaries”.

qualityStandard: Every tool used is inspected and fit for purpose before use.
Defective tools are tagged out and removed from the area.
The work area is clear and the workpiece is secured before force is applied.
documentationEvidence: Tool inspection record for the day, with any tool rejected and the reason
Record of the protection selected for each task
summary: Match the tool to the fastener, the material and the force.
Inspect each tool before use and reject defective ones.
Secure the work and choose protection from the actual task risks.

knowledgeChecks.question: An adjustable wrench has splayed jaws. What is the correct action?
options: Use it carefully because the job is almost done
Tag it out of service, replace it, and record the defect
Keep it in use and warn the client about the wrench's condition
Add extra force to hold the fitting while you tighten the nut

knowledgeChecks.question: Which factor should decide the protection a worker wears?
options: The risks identified for the actual task in the survey
What the worker prefers on the day, since comfort matters
The cheapest equipment available from the supplier this week
Whatever the client provided for the job at the start

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should a tool be left when it is not in use during work at height?
options: On the ladder rung for easy access during the job
In a bag or tray at ground level, not at height
On the window ledge above the work for easy reach
On the top step of a stepladder while you work
